about: The introitus of the formulary “Dedication of Saint Michael the Archangel” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

s01.translation: Bless the Lord, all His angels, you mighty in strength, who carry out His command, listening to the voice of His words. Bless the Lord, O my soul, and all that is within me, bless His holy name. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen. Bless the Lord, all His angels, you mighty in strength, who carry out His command, listening to the voice of His words.

w013.explanation: Ad with audiéndam expresses purpose: “to hear.” Audiéndam agrees with vocem in the feminine accusative singular.

w020.explanation: Bénedic takes Dómino in the Latin dative. English “bless” takes a direct object here: “the Lord.”

w026.explanation: Ómnia and quæ are plural in Latin, so the verb is sunt. English “all that” takes singular “is” in this collective reading.

w027.explanation: Nómini is the dative complement of the understood command to bless, parallel to Dómino. English uses “His holy name” as the direct object.
